functions.name: readModel
functions.purpose: Read a binary triangulated model and reconstruct its linked objects and attributes.
functions.float_sensitive_notes: No floating-point arithmetic; the binary format contains native structs, pointers and attributes, so compatibility depends on ABI, pointer size, layout, endianness and floating-point representation. Static helpers call updateAddressTree to reconstruct references.

functions.name: writeModel
functions.purpose: Write a triangulated model, its objects and attributes to a binary stream.
functions.float_sensitive_notes: No floating-point arithmetic; serialized native structs include pointer values and padding, making byte output dependent on process addresses, ABI, layout and endianness. Traversal order determines record order.

functions.name: updateAddressTree
functions.purpose: Insert or find an original address in a binary search tree and report whether it was already present.
functions.float_sensitive_notes: No floating-point arithmetic; pointer-to-off_t conversions and subtraction depend on platform widths and can produce implementation-dependent or undefined behavior.
functions.license_note: Comment credits the tree approach to Kernighan and Ritchie, The C Programming Language, 2nd edition, p. 139ff.

functions.name: main
functions.purpose: Provide conditional test entry points for reading and writing a model.
functions.float_sensitive_notes: The two definitions are both guarded by TEST, so enabling TEST defines main twice; the first also uses obsolete argument lists for readModel and writeModel. The signatures use implicit int and are definitions rather than full prototypes.
